To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the integration of contextual background knowledge in information assistance is possible, (ii) it can be implemented in a cognitive architecture and (iii) it can be evaluated by means of cognitive task analysis.
cognitive architectures can be used to provide a formalization of the human work domain and that this formalization can be used to support the assembly process in a smart assembly station.

(1) Cognitive architectures are a missing link between highly structured manufacturing systems and the implicit knowledge of the work domain; (2) The use of a cognitive architecture enables the development of an intelligent assistance system for assembly stations; (3) The use of the cognitive architecture Soar enables the implementation of an intelligent assembly assistance system in the domain of automotive manufacturing; (4) Soar is a cognitive architecture which is suitable for developing an intelligent assembly assistance systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an information assistant for assembly stations.
the development of an integrated system architecture for smart assembly stations which includes a knowledge-based information assistance system.
the integration and processing of contextual background knowledge in order to provide information assistance for smart assembly stations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a framework for information assistance in manufacturing, and we are able to show the potential of cognitive architectures for this application.
cognitive architectures can be used to provide assistance for assembly work in smart factories, but the research is still in an early stage.
the presented cognitive architectures are a promising approach to include background knowledge in the information assistance of assembly stations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a framework for the formalisation of contextual knowledge, its processing, and its application for information assistance.
we provide an information assistant for assembly stations that is based on the integration of contextual background knowledge and the cognitive capabilities of the Soar cognitive agent architecture.
cognitive architectures can be used to provide information assistance for assembly work in a more intelligent and flexible way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cognitive architectures can be used to formalise and implement contextual knowledge for information assistance.
cognitive architectures can be applied in the context of smart assembly stations to support human work processes in manufacturing.
cognitive architectures can be used for the formal representation of background knowledge in information assistance.
